title: Apply Theorem 10: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other
show: parallelogram ABCD with diagonals meeting at E, |AE|=3x+2 and |EC|=5x-4 marked

example.question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. The diagonals $[AC]$ and $[BD]$ meet at $E$. $|AE| = (3x + 2)$ cm and $|EC| = (5x - 6)$ cm. Find $x$ and $|AC|$.

steps.say: $E$ is where the diagonals cross. $\hl{1}{|AE|}$ and $\hl{2}{|EC|}$ are the two halves of the diagonal $[AC]$.
By Theorem 10, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. So $\hl{1}{|AE|} = \hl{2}{|EC|}$.
Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.
Put $x = 4$ into $|AE|$, then double it, because $E$ is the midpoint of $[AC]$.

title: Apply Corollary 4: A right angle at the circle stands on a diameter
show: circle with diameter AB, point C on circle, angle CAB=(2x+5)° and right angle at C

example.question: $[AB]$ is a diameter of a circle and $C$ is a point on the circle. $|\angle CAB| = (2x + 5)^\circ$ and $|\angle ABC| = (4x - 5)^\circ$. Find $x$ and $|\angle ABC|$.

steps.say: $[AB]$ is a diameter and $C$ is on the circle. By Corollary 4, the angle opposite the diameter is a right angle.
The three angles of triangle $ABC$ add to $180^\circ$. Write that with the $90^\circ$ you just found.
Collect like terms, then divide by $6$.

title: Apply Theorem 17: A diagonal bisects the area of a parallelogram
show: parallelogram PQRS with diagonal PR dividing it into two triangles, with area 420 m²

example.question: The area of the parallelogram $PQRS$ is $420$ m$^2$. (i) Find the area of the triangle $PQR$. (ii) $T$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$. Find the area of the triangle $PQT$.

steps.say: The diagonal $[PR]$ bisects the area of the parallelogram. So the triangle $PQR$ is half of $420$.
$T$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$, so $[PT]$ cuts triangle $PQR$ into two triangles with equal bases and the same height. Each is half of $210$.

title: Apply Theorem 18: Area of a parallelogram = base × height
show: parallelogram ABCD with base 12 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm marked

example.question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $|AB| = 12$ cm and the perpendicular distance between $[AB]$ and $[DC]$ is $6$ cm. $|BC| = 8$ cm. Find the area of $ABCD$, and the perpendicular distance between $[BC]$ and $[AD]$.

steps.say: Take $[AB]$ as the base. The height is the perpendicular distance to $[DC]$, which is $6$ cm.
Area of a parallelogram is base times perpendicular height.
The area does not change. Now take $[BC]$ as the base, with $|BC| = 8$, and let the new height be $h$.

title: Apply Theorem 16: Base × height is the same for every side of a triangle
show: parallelogram PQRS area 360 m² with T the midpoint of QR and triangle shaded

example.question:
$PQRS$ is a parallelogram with area $360\ \text{m}^2$. $T$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$.
(i) Find the area of the triangle $PQS$.
(ii) Find the area of the triangle $PQT$.

steps.say: Triangle $PQS$ has the same base $[PS]$ and the same height as the parallelogram. By Theorem 16 it is **half** the parallelogram.
Take $[QR]$ as the base. Triangle $PQR$ has the same base and height as the parallelogram, so its area is half again.
$T$ is the midpoint, so $|QT| = \tfrac{1}{2}|QR|$. The height from $P$ is the same, so triangle $PQT$ has **half** the area of $PQR$.

rows.aside: Same height, half the base: half the area.

title: Apply Theorem 20: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (and converse)
show: circle centre O radius 5 cm, tangent PT at T perpendicular to radius OT, |OP|=13 cm

example.question:
A circle has centre $O$ and radius $5$ cm. $[PT]$ is a tangent to the circle at $T$, and $|OP| = 13$ cm.
(i) Find $|PT|$.
(ii) Find the area of the triangle $OTP$.

steps.say: $[OT]$ is a radius and $[PT]$ is a tangent at $T$. By Theorem 20 they are perpendicular, so $|\angle OTP| = 90^\circ$.

rows.aside: Triangle $OTP$ is right-angled at $T$. $[OP]$ is the hypotenuse.

steps.say: Write Pythagoras with the numbers in, then solve for $|PT|$.
The two shorter sides are perpendicular, so use them as base and height.
